Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

locus

locus, locī m.

noun, second declension; plural locī (single spots, passages) and loca (places, a region)

place, position; post, standing; a passage of a book; position, state; room, a place for someone or something

In this lexicon

  • position

    the recommended word · classical · Cato Agr. 68: in suō quidque locō repōnitō

  • position

    also used · classical · Sall. C. 9 (Lewis & Short: locō cēdere, to leave one’s post)

  • section

    also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 1.7: locōs quōsdam trānsferam (Lewis & Short)

  • situation

    also used · classical · Verg. A. 2.322: quō rēs summa locō? (Lewis & Short)

  • space

    also used · classical · Plaut. Poen. 23: līberīs ut sit locus

  • locus ubi aedificātur: building site

    our formation

  • locus lūsōrius parvulōrum: playground

    modern

  • locus sēcrētus: restroom

    modern

  • locus harēnā plēnus ad lūdendum: sandpit

    our formation

Examples

  • omnia quīs ūsus erit, in suō quidque locō repōnitō

    put everything you will need back, each thing in its own placeCato Agr. 68

    In the entry for position

  • servī nē obsideant, līberīs ut sit locus

    slaves must not take up the seats, so that there is room for free menPlaut. Poen. 23
